name: container-pattern
context: A workload is packaged as an OCI/Docker image and deployed as one or more containers, and the design must exploit what containers make easy — layered images, filesystem and namespace isolation, per-container resource limits — rather than fight them. The named variations that matter are how containers are composed and specialised within one deployment unit: the init container, which runs to completion before the application container starts and exists to keep utilities out of the application image, to give a different filesystem view with access to secrets the app cannot see, and to block startup until preconditions are met; the sidecar container, which runs for the pod's lifetime and is implemented as an init container with restartPolicy: Always so the kubelet starts it before and terminates it after the application; the ambassador container, a sidecar specialisation whose sole job is to give the application a single stable interface to the outside world so the service behind it can be relocated without the consumer changing; and the adapter container, which translates data formats, protocols or APIs to interoperate with external services. Distinct from C4 logical containers, which are an organisational decomposition of a system into applications and data stores.
benefits: Layered images make distribution cheap: unchanged base and dependency layers are shared and cached, so only the application layer is pulled per release
Init containers let utility and setup code live in separate short-lived images, shrinking the attack surface of the application image without removing the tool
Different filesystem views per container, including access to secrets the application container cannot read, is a privilege boundary that virtual machines do not offer at this granularity
Startup ordering as a declarative guarantee: a pod is not Ready until every init container has succeeded, so application start can be gated on preconditions
Ambassador and adapter containers decouple the application from the location, protocol and shape of its dependencies without touching application code
Per-container resource requests and limits, plus pod-level QoS class, give precise scheduling and failure-domain control
One artifact runs identically on a laptop, in CI and in production, removing environment-specific configuration drift
tradeoffs: Init containers run to completion and cannot exchange messages with the app container; data flows one way, through files in a shared volume
Init container code must be idempotent because it may be restarted, retried or re-executed, and because a pod restart can re-run it

Resource accounting is counter-intuitive: the effective pod request for a resource is the higher of the sum of app containers and the highest init container, so an oversized init container reserves capacity for the pod's whole life
Init containers do not support lifecycle, livenessProbe, readinessProbe or startupProbe — readiness is implicitly 'exited successfully', which removes observability into what they are doing
Share-namespace composition couples the trust boundary: a compromised companion container reaches the application's ports and environment
Sidecar proliferation: a pod running many specialised containers multiplies memory cost and the number of things to operate
Images that bloat with build tooling and package caches destroy both pull speed and layer-cache efficiency
Container networking and storage still require separate platform primitives — a container is not a deployment, it is a packaging unit
use_cases: An application image that no longer carries sed, awk, dig or a package manager, because schema migration and wait-for-dependency logic moved into init containers
An OpenTelemetry collector shipped as a sidecar so the application image stays free of the tracing SDK
An ambassador container giving the application a stable localhost interface to a backing service that was relocated, so no application change was needed
An adapter container translating a legacy message-broker interface into an HTTP API so a new service can consume it without a client library
An init container granted access to secrets that the application container deliberately cannot read, then writing only the derived files the app needs
A gateway pod where init containers run migrations before the gateway container is allowed to start serving
avoid_when: The workload cannot tolerate container abstraction — hard real-time targets needing deterministic timing
The platform has no container runtime and no orchestration providing ordering and isolation semantics
The image must carry heavy proprietary tooling that cannot be separated into its own container
Init container resource reservations exceed what the node can schedule, making pods unschedulable for reasons invisible in the pod spec
A sidecar per instance would cost more than the functionality it offloads
component_types: Application container: the main workload image
Init container: a short-lived container that must exit successfully before the app container starts
Sidecar container: an init container with restartPolicy: Always that runs for the pod's lifetime alongside the app
Ambassador container: a sidecar providing a single stable interface to an external service
Adapter container: translating protocols, formats or APIs for interoperability
Layered image: ordered filesystem layers, each a cacheable diff, culminating in the application layer
Resource specification: requests and limits per container, aggregated into the pod's effective request and QoS class
Shared volume: emptyDir or similar, the only channel for one-way data from init containers to the app
anti_patterns: Baking utilities into the application image instead of using init containers, growing the attack surface for no benefit
Non-idempotent init container code that corrupts state when the pod restarts and the init container re-executes
Sidecar used as a place for domain logic, which recreates the coupling the decomposition was meant to remove
Unbounded init container resource requests that reserve node capacity for the entire pod lifetime
Container-per-microservice deployment where containers share a writable layer or assume local state that disappears on reschedule
latest tags in production, trading reproducibility for convenience
Ambassador sidecar whose interface mirrors the remote service exactly, defeating the indirection it was introduced for
No resource limits at all, which turns one misbehaving container into a node-wide incident
design_principles: Package once, run anywhere: the image is the unit of build, test and deployment, identical in every environment
Compose inside the deployment unit: init, sidecar, ambassador and adapter containers collaborate within one pod because they share a lifecycle and a network namespace
Separate by privilege and by lifetime: a short-lived setup task and a long-lived proxy have different security needs and belong in different images
Declare ordering rather than scripting it: pod semantics guarantee init completion and sidecar ordering so no application code coordinates startup
Keep the application image minimal: every tool left in the base image is attack surface and cache-invalidated weight
One-way data flow is the init container contract: hand off through files in a shared volume, not through messages
best_practices: Move setup, migration and wait-for-dependency logic out of the application image into dedicated init container images
Write init containers to be idempotent — they will be retried, and pod restarts re-execute them
Set CPU and memory requests and limits on every container, remembering that the pod's effective request is the higher of the app-container sum and the highest init container
Use native sidecar semantics (initContainers with restartPolicy: Always) so kubelet handles ordering and shutdown
Order init containers deliberately and use activeDeadlineSeconds to stop them blocking pod readiness forever
Build layered, minimal, multi-stage images and pin digests or immutable tags rather than using latest
Give init containers a filesystem view with access to the secrets they need and without access to anything the application should not read
Prefer an ambassador or adapter container over embedding a client library when the dependency must be relocatable or protocol-translated
